digest.component_or_area: test infrastructure — subprocess and network sentinels
propositions: Five ACLI subprocess reap tests each burn ~1.01s waiting for a blanket 1s autouse fixture deadline to expire, creating unnecessary test latency.
The same blanket fixture caps a rate-limit backoff test that requires two sequential spawns to complete, creating a latent load-dependent flake in the opposite direction.

Three reap tests assert on child-side events (pidfile, spawn counter, flushed output) whose ordering depends only on the injected window exceeding interpreter startup time, creating a wall-clock race that smaller windows lose on loaded runners.
The snapshot stall test injects a 2s low-speed window when its sibling already proves git honors 1s, wasting test execution time.
Reap test ordering must be made explicit via readiness markers rather than tuned by picking a larger deadline number, to eliminate real-time dependencies.
